chunks: 554 - And ʿUmar ibn Yazīd said: I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, "May salat be performed on behalf of the deceased?" So he said:

“Yes, such that he may indeed be in hardship, then Allah relieves that hardship from him; then he is approached and it is said to him: ‘This hardship has been lightened from you by the salat of so-and-so, your brother, on your behalf.’”
He said: So I said to him, “May I include two men together in two rakʿahs?” He said, “Yes.”
And he عليه السلام said: “Indeed, the deceased rejoices in mercy being invoked for him and in seeking forgiveness for him, just as the living rejoices in a gift presented to him.

And it is permissible for a man to assign his hajj, or his ʿumrah, or some of his salat, or some of his tawaf, to some of his close ones while he is deceased, and he benefits from it, such that he may even be one who is under displeasure and then he is forgiven, or be under constraint and then it is expanded for him. And the deceased is informed of that. Even if a man were to do that on behalf of a nāṣib, it would be lightened for him. Piety, maintaining ties, and hajj may be assigned to the deceased and the living; as for salat, it is not permissible on behalf of the living.”

key_terms.الْمَيِّتِ: the deceased person who receives benefit from deeds performed on his behalf
key_terms.بِصَلَاةِ: through salat performed on behalf of another
key_terms.حَجَّتَهُ: one’s hajj offered on behalf of another
key_terms.ضِيقٍ: hardship or constriction affecting the deceased
key_terms.طَوَافِهِ: one’s tawaf assigned for another’s benefit
key_terms.نَاصِبٍ: a hostile opponent of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام

ai.seo_question: Can salat, hajj, or other acts of worship be performed on behalf of a deceased person in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith states that acts of worship performed on behalf of the deceased benefit them, bringing relief, forgiveness, and joy in the barzakh. It also distinguishes between what may be gifted to the dead and living, clarifying that salat may be performed for the deceased but not on behalf of the living.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.554 - Omar ibn Yazid said: I asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) whether it is permissible to pray on behalf of a deceased person.

Imam (as) replied: "Yes, even to the extent that if the deceased is in difficulty, Allah (swt) will alleviate that difficulty through the prayer of his brother for him. Then it is said to the deceased, 'Your difficulty has been eased by the prayer of such-and-such, your brother, on your behalf.'"

I then asked: "Can I include two people in one set of two units of prayer?"
Imam (as) replied: "Yes."
He (as) also said: "The deceased rejoices in mercy and forgiveness offered on his behalf just as the living person rejoices in a gift given to him."

[AL SADUQ]
It is permissible to perform pilgrimage (Hajj or Umrah), prayer, or circumambulation (Tawaf) on behalf of a deceased person, and they benefit from it—even if the deceased was under divine displeasure, they may be forgiven or have their hardship relieved through such actions. The deceased is made aware of these acts. Even performing these acts for an adversary (nāṣib) could lessen their burden. Acts of piety, connection, and Hajj can be performed for both the living and the dead, but prayer on behalf of a living person is not permitted.
